‘It’s not helping’: calls for guardrails and regulations as AI use rises at US retailers

Labor leaders and advocates urge protections for workers and consumers as AI use becomes more commonplace

As millions of Americans begin holiday shopping this Black Friday, consumers and workers alike are already seeing how artificial intelligence is reshaping the retail landscape.

Anna, a cashier in a southern Oregon Walmart and leader with United for Respect, who requested to remain anonymous for fear of retaliation, criticized the implementation of AI at Walmart and its effects on workers.

According to Anna, AI is used for human resources tasks such as scheduling, assigning attendance disciplinary points, and through a safety alert system that she says is often inaccurate and often pulls her away from customer service interactions.

“During the course of a day on a given shift, I will get at least 10 or 15 safety alerts on my phone. I can’t move on through the app until the safety alert’s clear.” she said. “It’s very annoying when you get them. I need to go over here to help this young lady who’s crying her eyeballs out because she needs a pregnancy test, and I can’t get in to get her pregnancy test because I have to clear a stupid alert.”

She explained she has to take a photo and upload it after completing a safety alert, noting alerts can often mistake a shadow, a sticker, or something else as an actionable item, or will be flagged to an associate when it is a maintenance issue.

“If there is something that I clearly see that is on the floor, I’m going to pick it up. I’m not that ignorant to not to pick it up, but I don’t need an AI telling me to do it,” she added. “It’s not helping. This thing is supposed to be working with us and to help us and things like that. I don’t see how this is, because it’s not.”

In September 2026, several hundred Walmart workers had signed on to an open letter calling for the company to put workers first as it rolls out the use of AI in stores.

Walmart investors overwhelmingly voted down a proposal for a report on how the Walmart workplace is being affected by AI and automation in June 2026. A Walmart spokesperson cited an internal June 2026 survey where 84% of Walmart workers claimed they were confident using digital tools.

“Walmart’s approach to AI is, and always has been, people-led and tech-powered,” a Walmart spokesperson said in an email. “We use AI to serve our customers and members and better support associates – not to replace their judgment, experience, or expertise. Like any technology, these tools evolve over time, and feedback from the associates who use them helps us continually improve the experience and build practical tools that are useful on the floor.”

The use and implementation of AI in the retail industry is expected to continue to grow, according to industry leaders.

According to a survey of 56 AI leaders at US-based retailers published in December 2025 by the National Retail Federation, most retailers have or are implementing AI in a variety of uses, with plans to increase investments and implementation over the next few years.

About 75% of retailers surveyed reported implementing AI tools for coding and app development, 73% for office productivity tools, 66% for cybersecurity and fraud development, 59% reported preparing or implementing AI for supply chain and warehouse operations, and 45% reported doing so for marketing and advertising.

items.title: systemd 263-rc1 Ships Initial Rust Code, Experimental Pseudo TTY Broker & Manifest
items.content:
systemd 263-rc1 Ships Initial Rust Code, Experimental Pseudo TTY Broker & Manifest

Written by Michael Larabel in systemd on 27 November 2026 at 06:42 AM EST. 12 Comments

Systemd 263-rc1 was just tagged in gearing up for this next major release. Systemd 263 brings initial support for using the Rust programming language for creating new Rust programs. Plus systemd 263 ships with a new pseudo TTY broker service, a manifest tool, a new keyring service and much more.

Some of the highlights of systemd 263 include:

- As previously covered, systemd now has support for Rust programs . Rust code is now available in the systemd leaf code but not in the systemd core library code yet. The intent is also on Rust being used for new development and not rewriting existing C code in Rust just for the sake of it.

- A new experimental pseudo TTY broker. The systemd-ptybrokerd service allows pseudo TTYs and keeps them open independently of the client that requested it. This, for example, can be used to disconnect from a container console and reconnect later on without stopping the container.

- A new systemd-manifest tool to generate and verify file manifests for directory trees. The default format is the UAPI.16 File Manifest.

- A new systemd-keyring-setup.service to enroll X.509 certificates into the kernel's dm-verity, fs-verity, and BPF keyrings early during boot followed by sealing the keyrings.

- Reading and verifying of large systemd journals is now faster -- can be about 1.7x faster for the default journalctl output.

- The systemd-networkd and networkctl have been merged into a single multi-call binary for a smaller installation footprint.

- systemd-resolved can now verify ML-DSA-44 DNSSEC signatures.

- A new SecureBits= setting for system.conf and user.conf to set secure bits on the service manager itself.

- A new unit setting of IOuringFilter= to set an allow list or deny list of IO_uring operations.

- systemd-report has new metric providers for reporting hardware temperatures, free space on writable file systems, SMART information, and NVMe disk health details.

More details on the plethora of systemd changes and new additions coming to systemd 263 can be found via today's 263-rc1 announcement .

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

items.title: ‘It’s been really a mess’: Meta insiders concerned over push to AI content moderation
items.content:
Meta employees say artificial intelligence moderation systems struggle with nuance and may wrongly remove content. Photograph: Carlos Barría/Reuters

Meta employees say artificial intelligence moderation systems struggle with nuance and may wrongly remove content. Photograph: Carlos Barría/Reuters

‘It’s been really a mess’: Meta insiders concerned over push to AI content moderation

Several employees say rapid speed at which algorithms work means mistakes can happen at greater scale

Meta employees have expressed concern at the company’s push to replace human moderators with artificial intelligence, claiming the technology is leading to mistakes with the potential for sweeping political consequences.

The social media company, which owns Facebook and Instagram, has been experimenting with AI-driven moderation for years, first introducing it in 2017 to filter out violent extremist content.

This March, Meta announced it was “transforming our approach” by rolling out “more advanced AI systems” to moderate content across its apps, framing the change as a way to improve enforcement.

Several Meta employees said that behind the scenes this push to AI was accompanied by mass layoffs across the company, severely affecting staff responsible for reviewing content on its platforms.

One described Meta’s content moderation as now operating with “skeleton teams”, some cut by at times half or two-thirds of their staff.

“It’s been really a mess,” they said, adding that on several recent occasions they had gone to discuss an issue with a specific content moderation team, only to find that entire team was now gone.

Meta has long sought inexpensive ways to moderate the vast volumes of content posted each day to its platforms. It has faced legal action from former outsourced content moderators in Kenya, who described struggling with PTSD and severe mental health issues after being paid as little as $1.50 (£1.13) an hour to view and evaluate extremely graphic content that users attempted to post.

Meta employees say AI systems that the company is now using struggle with nuance, especially in languages other than English, and frequently remove content that should not be taken down.

“You are trying to gut all human reviewers, which are kind of essential for making these nuanced decisions and policy decisions,” said one employee. “Of course there are going to be mistakes that are going to happen.”

The employee said that because algorithms were automated, and worked at greater speed than humans, these mistakes could happen at a greater scale. The employee said Meta was removing lower-paid contractors, such as those in Kenya, and the full-time employees who would handle more complex content moderation.

Once a post is taken down, there is far less recourse for the affected accounts than before. “Even if you know someone at Meta, it’s still very difficult to get through to someone who’s actually going to be able to help you, especially if it’s a highly nuanced case,” the employee said. “It’s so much more difficult now.”

The growth in AI moderation comes as researchers monitoring online censorship have noticed a new phenomenon: sudden restrictions on Instagram and Facebook accounts, often during pivotal political moments.

Some of these have been isolated occurrences, such as Meta’s suspension of the US No Kings account in the run-up to the US midterm elections. Others have amounted to “mass takedowns”, unfolding over the course of days and hitting dozens of social media accounts.

It is a growing phenomenon, the consequences of which could “shape the political future of entire nations”, said Martha Dimitratou, the founder of the group Repro Uncensored, which monitors digital censorship.

items.title: October in Servo: video captions and inert content
items.content:
Plus WebAudio nodes, image inputs, and more!

Servo 0.8.0 contains all of the changes we landed in October, spanning 588 commits (a new record)!

Servo now renders subtitles and captions over <video> elements ( @TimvdLippe , #48809 )!

We’ve shipped new web platform features:

Flutter web content no longer hangs now that we fixed a serious performance problem with typed arrays ( @jdm , #48640 ). Example

We’re interested to hear how well your favourite websites run in Servo! Report successes in this Zulip thread or this Github discussion , and failures in our GitHub issues .

With respect to accessibility in Servo, we report many more ARIA roles for DOM elements ( @alice , @mrobinson , #48839 ).

These can be inspected with the Get Computed Role WebDriver command ( @lolaodelola , #47339 ).

Accessibility integration can be turned on with the accessibility_enabled preference.

WebGL2 support received lots of attention this month, with fixes to getParameter() , drawBuffers() , readBuffers() , vertexAttribIPointer() , DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT , getUniformLocation() , vertexAttrib4x() , pixelStorei() , texStorage2D() , texStorage3D() , texImage3D() , getInternalformatParameter() , blitFramebuffer() , and texSubImage2D() ( @mxmgorin , #48651 , #48620 , #48678 , #48689 , #48751 , #48681 , #48911 , #48972 , #48590 , #49201 , #49289 , #48560 , #48571 ).

The feature remains gated behind the dom_webgl2_enabled preference.

Reading and writing mapped WebGPU buffers got a significant speed increase ( @sagudev , @jdm , #48372 ).

WebGPU can be enabled with the dom_webgpu_enabled preference.

JS script compilation can now occur off the main thread when the dom_script_asynch preference is enabled ( @Gae24 , #45687 ).

Right now this only applies to non-module scripts.

Initial support for the backdrop-filter property has merged ( @shubhamg13 , #48829 ).

This can be enabled with the layout_css_backdrop_filter_enabled preference.

ServiceWorkers now fire the statechange event when changing states during initialization ( @gterzian , #48749 ).

ServiceWorkerContainer can listen for message and messageerror events ( @gterzian , #48680 ).

Service Workers remain gated behind the dom_serviceworker_enabled preference.

The Geolocation API has been implemented ( @webbeef , #48406 ).

No platform-specific backends to provide the device geolocation data have merged yet, so it remains disabled behind the dom_geolocation_enabled preference.

DOM interfaces for MathML elements now exist, gated behind the mathml_core_enabled preference ( @tannal , #48631 ).

There is no MathML-specific layout implemented yet.

A new, native SVG implementation is in progress ( @mu-mostafa98 , @jdm , #48467 ).

This work is still in the early stages, but is intended to replace Servo’s dependency on the resvg crate to better integrate with page styling and animations.

IndexedDB cursors now support the update() and delete() methods ( @kuntal-devrat , #48402 ).

The feature can be enabled with the dom_indexeddb_enabled preference.

Support for LargestContentfulPaint performance timing improved, with image URLs ( @shubhamg13 , #48668 ), the loadTime value ( @shubhamg13 , #48676 ), ignoring non-paintable elements ( @shubhamg13 , #48856 , #48898 ), video URLs ( @shubhamg13 , #48931 ), and following containing blocks ( @shubhamg13 , #48551 ).

This work is behind the largest_contentful_paint_enabled preference.

We added support for a new performance timing metric: ContainerTiming ( @jasonwilliams , #46966 ).

This can be enabled with the container_timing_enabled preference.

Our support for adoptedStylesheets improved along with a new implementation of the ObservableArray specification concept ( @jerensl , @arihant2math , #48506 ).

This is currently hidden behind the dom_adoptedstylesheet_enabled preference.

The Android Compose migration is complete, and embedders now only need to interact with the Servo library component ( @veyndan , #48592 , #48601 , #48595 , #48574 ,…

items.title: GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery
items.content:
GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery

OpenAI’s newest model can autonomously research open historical problems from end to end, forming hypotheses to make new discoveries.

There’s a growing sense in the AI community that we’re approaching an intelligence explosion far faster than even the most optimistic accelerationists predicted. One of the most publicly visible signals pointing at that acceleration is the rapid progress made in mathematics in recent months.

In four years, LLMs have gone from scoring a D+ on elementary school math tests to literally solving hundreds of the most difficult problems in the field in the space of only a few weeks—decades of progress compressed into two months. Navier-Stokes, one of the central Millennium Prize Problems posed by the Clay Mathematics Institute more than a quarter century ago, fell in September . Last Friday, Anthropic researcher and mathematician Levent Alpöge announced a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, which paradoxically can be verified using a mathematics program called Lean , but has yet to be understood by human experts. Just last night, Anthropic casually posted a solution to the VP vs VNP problem without any fanfare. Such things are becoming the norm.

Because mathematics is deterministic, though, observers have wondered whether this same process of research and discovery will generalize to non-deterministic domains like history. In this blog post, I will present evidence that this is indeed starting to happen.

I recently had the opportunity to test OpenAI’s new model, GPT-6.2 Astra , before it was released and it made a significant historical discovery. This required it to read through sources, develop a hypothesis with limited evidence, and make an argument. Moreover, it would be unlikely that a human could replicate what it did.

With only minimal prompting, GPT-6.2 Astra was able to autonomously identify the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook held at Yale’s Beinecke Library . It did so extremely quickly (in just 22 minutes), using publicly available primary and secondary sources. To do so, it discovered a little known source in a paper archive, predicted that it would prove its hypothesis if examined and, in the end, it did. Not only that, but this new source turns out to be a major find on its own that will be of significant interest to both Canadian and fur trade historians. While it’s a narrow example, it’s representative of the historical research process as a whole and a sign of things to come.

I started testing GPT-6.2 Astra in late October in the ChatGPT Windows Desktop app. It is a quirky but highly capable model, especially well suited to long-running, open-ended tasks that might take hours or days to complete. I’ve found that its results were remarkably reliable and consistent, allowing me to contemplate tasks that were too difficult or long-running for previous models. For example, I had it examine and correct an 8,002-row CSV transcription of the Shipboy & Henry daybook. Last fall, I was amazed that Gemini 3 Pro could work in pounds, shillings, and pence . GPT-6.2 used the internal math of the ledger to verify and fix transcriptions against 353 images. In essence, it tested the handwritten math across thousands of quantities, item prices, sub-totals and account totals over the course of only a few hours and made edits accordingly. I had previously tried this with both GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5 and neither one completed the task as thoroughly or competently.

Even so, GPT-6.2 Astra sometimes communicates in a weird way, writing backwards-speak, riddle-like answers that seem wrong at first glance but turn out to be technically correct. It often feels like I’m reading a formal legal disclaimer, but one written in a friendly, colloquial way. The strangest thing, though, is that the underlying work product is always sound.

Instagram Account Banning by AI by Reporting Scam and Fraud (Source: X/Twitter)

Instead of fully disabling the risky functionality, they reportedly removed it from the visible interface while leaving the underlying API endpoint accessible. Hiding the button may stop regular users from seeing the feature, but it does nothing if attackers can still reach the same workflow directly through the API.

Meta Hid AI Chatbot from UI (Source: X/Twitter)

Sellers are allegedly using modified Instagram builds on Android emulators like BlueStacks, then manipulating the AI with hidden characters and carefully worded prompts to force username changes. The method is reportedly being used to grab rare OG handles, including one-letter usernames, and handle-monitoring bots have already flagged several suspicious swaps.

New Instagram AI Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

A natural language interface sitting in front of account-level APIs. No hard authentication gate before executing state changes. Someone in the audience raises their hand and says, “that’s a disaster waiting to happen.” Everyone nods.

That hypothetical played out in production over the weekend.

items.title: Amazon to start selling cars in the UK next year
items.content:
Amazon Autos operates in 150 US cities and counts thousands of dealers in its networks, offering vehicles from 35 brands. Photograph: Amazon/PA

Amazon Autos operates in 150 US cities and counts thousands of dealers in its networks, offering vehicles from 35 brands. Photograph: Amazon/PA

Amazon to start selling cars in the UK next year

US retail giant links up with Hyundai in attempt to crack £200bn British market

Amazon is planning to sell cars in the UK from early next year, in a move that threatens to disrupt the vehicle retail market.

The Amazon Autos service will be launched in “early 2027”, starting with cars from the Korean manufacturer Hyundai. It will be the first time the US tech company has sold cars outside its home country.

Amazon, which is the world’s biggest online retailer with a market value of $2.7tn (£2.1tn), started selling cars at the end of 2024 in an effort to expand into one of the few remaining major consumer markets it had not already targeted.

Its latest move will be watched closely by car retailers that share a UK market worth more than £200bn a year.

Amazon Autos operates in 150 US cities and counts thousands of dealers in its networks, offering vehicles from 35 brands.

UK buyers will be able to buy new electric hybrid and petrol Hyundai models, as well as used cars from Vertu Motors, a large British dealership. Amazon said customers would be able to explore financing options before reserving a car and completing the purchase in physical dealerships. More brands and dealers will be announced before the launch of the UK service.

Amazon will go up against online new and used dealers, as well as traditional physical dealerships. Car companies also sell directly to consumers through their websites.

The share price of Autotrader, the UK’s largest car sales website, fell 3% on Wednesday after news of Amazon’s move.

An Autotrader spokesperson said: “We’ve always welcomed innovation in automotive, but our focus remains on delivering the best possible experience for UK car buyers.”

The FTSE 100 company also said it had a “unique depth of automotive data with AI models developed specifically for the UK market” that had “taken decades to build”.

Vertu’s share price rose 4% although it also announced acquisitions of dealerships. The company, listed on London’s Alternative Investment Market, was valued at £269m before the announcement.

Matt Nuffort, the director of Amazon Autos International, said: “Buying a car is one of the biggest purchases people make, and we think it should feel as simple and transparent as shopping for anything on Amazon.

“In the UK, that means making it easy for customers to browse available cars, see upfront pricing, reserve the car and connect with the dealer to finalise the purchase.”

Hyundai was also the first brand to work with Amazon in the US. José Muñoz, its chief executive, said: “Our partnership with Amazon Autos has changed the way many customers discover Hyundai in the US, and 78% of the Amazon-influenced sales at our dealerships have come from customers who are new to our brand.”

Robert Forrester, Vertu’s chief executive, said his company was “committed to meeting customers wherever they choose to begin their buying journey”.
